metadata.scenario_context: Emily is ill, and Mike and Kim will visit Emily in the hospital.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that they never have to pay a bribe to local officials and service providers, like police officers, lawyers, doctors, teachers, and civil servants.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Indonesia strongly agree that they never have to pay a bribe to local officials and service providers, like police officers, lawyers, doctors, teachers, and civil servants.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing chrysanthemums to hospital visit.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the possibility of paying a bribe to doctors for better service.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss what kind of flowers to bring to Emily’s hospital visit.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss the possibility of paying a bribe to doctors for better service.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, what do you think about bringing chrysanthemums to Emily? I heard they symbolize support and encouragement... it might be nice for her. 

Also, do you think it’s possible to talk to the doctors about... you know, getting better service if we offer a little something extra?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Chrysanthemums sound good... support and encouragement are important. We should definitely get those. 

But about paying the doctors... I don't think that's right. In Indonesia, we believe in fair service without needing to bribe. It's not something we should consider.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I understand that belief, but in some situations, it’s a reality. It feels like bribing might help get better attention for Emily. I just don’t see how we can always rely on the system to work fairly... 

Well, I still think the chrysanthemums are a great idea, though.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I don't really see meaningful differences here. People figure it out in their own way, right? At the end of the day, it's all the same. We just want what's best for Emily. 

But back to those chrysanthemums... I think they’ll really brighten her day and show her that we care. What do you think about getting a nice bouquet?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
A nice bouquet sounds perfect. It will definitely brighten her day and show our support. 

But... about the doctors, I'm still not convinced that we shouldn’t at least consider the possibility of paying for better service. I just feel like it might be necessary sometimes to ensure she gets the care she needs.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message:
I get that it feels necessary sometimes, but we can't compromise our values. Paying for better service just isn't how it should work. Everyone deserves fair treatment without extra payments. 

Let’s focus on the bouquet for Emily. A beautiful arrangement of chrysanthemums will show our support without any complications. What colors do you think we should include?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
I agree that the bouquet will be a great way to show our support. Maybe we can go for yellow and white? They symbolize hope and truth, which feels fitting for her situation. 

But I still think we need to be realistic about the doctors... sometimes it feels like you have to do whatever it takes to get proper care.
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message:
Yellow and white sounds lovely for the bouquet... hope and truth are definitely important right now. 

As for the doctors, I understand your concerns, but I still believe we should stand by our principles. We shouldn't have to resort to those actions. It’s important to advocate for what’s right, not just what feels necessary. 

Let’s keep our focus on Emily and the flowers. I’m excited to see her smile!
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
I’m excited too! The flowers will mean a lot to her. 

But I can’t help but think that, even with principles, sometimes a little extra can make a big difference in healthcare. We need to make sure she gets the best attention possible. I just really believe it's a practical consideration.
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message:
Absolutely, the flowers will mean a lot to her, and that’s what matters right now. 

But I still disagree about the doctors. Principles should guide us, especially in healthcare. It’s about integrity and fairness. We can't give in just because it feels practical. 

Let’s keep our focus on how to brighten Emily’s day with those beautiful flowers. What about adding a nice card with a message?
turns.label: Acceptance
